It is the collection of a menu button: it takes the trigger's results, focuses the first or last item as the trigger says, chooses with Enter, Space and clicks, closes the menu, and the focus returns to the trigger by the scope of the trigger's MenuProps (UseMenu adds none).

Call it in the component that is rendered while the menu is open: it focuses an item when it mounts, so a menu that stays mounted while closed would not focus again.

```go
mt := aria.UseMenuTrigger(aria.MenuTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: mt.Ref, Ref: mt.MenuRef, Open: mt.Open, OnClose: mt.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Modal: true,
})
return Fragment(
    Button(mt.TriggerProps, Text("Actions")),
    Portal(If(mt.Open, tela.C(actionMenu, mt, pop))))

type actionMenu struct{ mt aria.MenuTriggerResult; pop aria.PopoverResult }

func (m actionMenu) Build() tela.Node {
    menu := aria.UseMenu(aria.MenuOptions[string]{
        Keys: actions, TextValue: strings.ToUpper,
        OnAction: run, OnClose: m.mt.Close,
        AutoFocus: true, FocusStrategy: m.mt.FocusStrategy, Ref: m.mt.MenuRef,
    })
    return Div(m.pop.Props, m.mt.MenuProps, menu.Props, Class("w-48 rounded-md border bg-popover p-1"),
        h.Range(len(actions), func(i int) tela.Node {
            return Div(menu.ItemProps(actions[i]), Key(actions[i]),
                Class("rounded px-2 py-1.5 focus-visible:bg-accent aria-disabled:opacity-50"), Text(actions[i]))
        }))
}
```

Items with SelectionMode "single" or "multiple" are radio and checkbox items: they print as `menuitemradio "Name" [checked]` and `menuitemcheckbox "Name" [checked]`, and `aria-checked:` styles them. The mouse focuses the item under it, as in a native menu. Disabled items are skipped. Submenus are not part of this hook.

**Example**

```go
// A menu button: ArrowDown opens the menu with the first item focused,
// Enter chooses it, the menu closes and the focus goes back.
var ev events
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, menuApp(aria.MenuOptions[string]{}, &ev), telatest.Size(400, 300))
trigger := telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions")
app.Focus(trigger)
app.Press("ArrowDown")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Enter")
app.ExpectFocused(trigger)
fmt.Println(ev.take())
// Output:
// - menu "Actions":
//   - menuitem "Edit"
//   - menuitem "Duplicate"
//   - menuitem "Archive"
//   - menuitem "Delete"
// action:edit
```

### type MenuTriggerOptions

```go
type MenuTriggerOptions struct {
    // Trigger is how a pointer opens the menu: "press" (the default), at
    // the press of a mouse or a pen and at the release of a touch, or
    // "longPress", when the press lasts, which leaves the quick press of the
    // trigger to OnPress; the keyboard then opens it with Alt+ArrowDown and
    // Alt+ArrowUp only. Another value panics in dev mode.
    Trigger string
    // Type is what the trigger opens: "menu" (the default) or "listbox".
    Type string
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled menu; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called
    // with the next state: for a controlled menu it is how the change is
    // asked for, for an uncontrolled one a notification.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled makes the trigger inert and disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // OnPress is the trigger's own press with Trigger "longPress"; it does
    // not run after a long press that opened the menu.
    OnPress func(PressEvent)
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and MenuRef the menu's, for hooks used
    // together with others on the same element; the zero value makes the
    // hook create its own.
    Ref, MenuRef tela.ElementRef
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MenuTriggerOptions configures [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger).

### type MenuTriggerResult

```go
type MenuTriggerResult struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the trigger: the press (and long press), the
    // keyboard that opens the menu, the "button" role, a tab stop,
    // aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and, while open, aria-controls.
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // MenuProps go to the menu's element: the ref, aria-labelledby (the
    // trigger) and a focus scope that gives the focus back to the trigger
    // when the menu closes. The menu's other hooks and [UsePopover] share
    // MenuRef.
    MenuProps tela.Prop
    // Open is whether the menu is open.
    Open bool
    // FocusStrategy is where the focus goes when the menu opens: [FocusFirst],
    // [FocusLast], or "" for the menu itself (opened with a mouse or a
    // touch). The menu focuses accordingly when it mounts.
    FocusStrategy string
    // SetOpen asks for a state, Toggle for the other one and Close for
    // closed. A menu closes itself when an item is chosen by calling Close.
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Toggle  func()
    Close   func()
    // Pressed is true while the trigger is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and MenuRef the menu's.
    Ref, MenuRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

MenuTriggerResult is what [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger) returns.

#### func UseMenuTrigger

```go
func UseMenuTrigger(o MenuTriggerOptions) MenuTriggerResult
```

UseMenuTrigger holds the open state of a menu and returns the props of its trigger (React Aria's useMenuTrigger with useMenuTriggerState): a press opens it, and so do Enter, Space and ArrowDown (focusing the first item) and ArrowUp (the last), or a long press with Trigger "longPress".

```go
mt := aria.UseMenuTrigger(aria.MenuTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: mt.Ref, Ref: mt.MenuRef, Open: mt.Open, OnClose: mt.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Modal: true,
})
return Fragment(
    Button(mt.TriggerProps, Text("Actions")),
    Portal(If(mt.Open, Div(pop.Props, mt.MenuProps, Role("menu"), ...))))
```

The menu itself, its items and keyboard navigation belong to the menu collection hook (UseMenu); this hook gives it the focus strategy and Close, to call when an item is chosen.

**Example**

```go
// ArrowDown opens the menu focusing its first item, ArrowUp its last.
page := func() tela.Node {
    mt := aria.UseMenuTrigger(aria.MenuTriggerOptions{})
    pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
        Trigger: mt.Ref, Ref: mt.MenuRef, Open: mt.Open, OnClose: mt.Close, Placement: "bottom-start", Modal: true,
    })
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(mt.TriggerProps, Class("absolute left-4 top-4 h-8 w-24"), Text("Actions")),
        Portal(If(mt.Open,
            Div(pop.Props, mt.MenuProps, Role("menu"), Class("w-40 bg-white"),
                Textf("focus the %s item", mt.FocusStrategy)))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions"))
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.ExpectText("focus the first item")
app.Press("Escape")
app.Press("ArrowUp")
app.ExpectText("focus the last item")
fmt.Println("ArrowDown: first, ArrowUp: last")
// Output: ArrowDown: first, ArrowUp: last
```

### type OffsetOptions

```go
type OffsetOptions struct {
    // CrossAxis moves the element along the anchor's edge, so that it
    // skids away from the alignment (Floating UI's crossAxis). Positive
    // moves it right for the top and bottom sides, down for the left and
    // right ones (mirrored in a right-to-left element for the top and
    // bottom sides).
    CrossAxis float32
    // AlignmentAxis replaces CrossAxis for aligned placements ("-start",
    // "-end") when HasAlignmentAxis is set: positive moves the element
    // toward the inside of the anchor's edge from the start and, negated,
    // from the end (Floating UI's alignmentAxis, which is a number or null).
    AlignmentAxis    float32
    HasAlignmentAxis bool
}
```

OffsetOptions are the options of [`Offset`](#func-offset) beyond the distance.

### type OverlayOptions

```go
type OverlayOptions struct {
    // Open is whether the overlay is open. A closed overlay is not on the
    // overlay stack: its Props do nothing. Render the overlay only while
    // it is open, and pass the same value here, or true when the
    // component that calls the hook exists only while the overlay does.
    Open bool
    // OnClose is called when the user asks to close the overlay: Escape,
    // a press outside it (with Dismissable) or the focus leaving it (with
    // ShouldCloseOnBlur). The caller closes it, by changing the state that
    // Open comes from.
    OnClose func()
    // Dismissable closes the overlay with a press outside it: at the
    // pointer down, the press is kept from the elements under it, and at
    // the release OnClose is called and the click the press would make is
    // cancelled (React Aria's isDismissable). An alert dialog is not
    // dismissable.
    Dismissable bool
    // KeyboardDismissDisabled keeps Escape from closing the overlay. The
    // overlay still takes the key while it is the top one: Escape does not
    // reach the overlays below it nor the page.
    KeyboardDismissDisabled bool
    // ShouldCloseOnBlur closes the overlay when the focus moves from
    // inside it to another element outside it (not when it goes nowhere,
    // such as the window losing the focus).
    ShouldCloseOnBlur bool
    // ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside decides, for a press outside the
    // overlay, whether it closes it; nil closes it for every press. The
    // event carries the position of the press in the window: a popover
    // excludes its trigger by comparing it with the trigger's bounds. It
    // applies to Dismissable overlays.
    ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside func(tela.PointerEvent) bool
    // Modal makes everything outside the overlay inert while it is open
    // and the topmost modal overlay (the overlays opened from it stay
    // usable): it cannot be pressed or focused, is out of the Tab order and
    // is hidden from the aria snapshot (React Aria's ariaHideOutside).
    // A dialog is modal; a popover, a menu or a toast usually is not.
    Modal bool
}
```

OverlayOptions configures [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay).

### type OverlayResult

```go
type OverlayResult struct {
    // Props go to the overlay's element: they put it on the overlay stack
    // while it is mounted and Open, so that Escape and presses outside
    // reach only the top overlay, and make it modal if asked.
    Props tela.Prop
}
```

OverlayResult is what [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay) returns.

#### func UseOverlay

```go
func UseOverlay(o OverlayOptions) OverlayResult
```

UseOverlay returns the props that make an element an overlay (React Aria's useOverlay and, with Modal, useModalOverlay): the topmost one is closed by Escape and by a press outside it, and a modal one makes the rest of the window inert. Overlays opened from inside another count as inside it (a popover in a dialog, in a Portal or not), so pressing in the popover does not close the dialog, and Escape closes the popover first.

```go
func Confirm(open bool, close func()) tela.Node {
    ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{Open: open, OnClose: close, Dismissable: true, Modal: true})
    return Portal(Presence(If(open,
        Div(ov.Props, Exit("opacity-0"), Class("... transition starting:opacity-0"), ...))))
}
```

Use [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) on the same element for the dialog role and the focus, and [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger) for the state and the trigger. Rendering it inside a Presence lets it fade out: an exiting overlay is inert and no longer on the stack, so the page below is usable at once and a second Escape reaches the next overlay.

The hook has no ref: [`FocusScopeOptions.Ref`](#type-focusscopeoptions) and the other hooks that share the element take theirs as usual.

**Example**

```go
// A modal overlay: Escape and a press outside close it, and the page
// below is inert while it is open.
page := func() tela.Node {
    open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
    ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{
        Open: open, OnClose: func() { setOpen.Set(false) }, Dismissable: true, Modal: true,
    })
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(Class("h-8 w-24"), Text("Page")),
        If(open, Div(ov.Props, Class("absolute left-[100px] top-[100px] h-20 w-40 bg-white"), Text("Overlay"))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Escape")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - text: Overlay
// - button "Page"
```

### type OverlayTriggerOptions

```go
type OverlayTriggerOptions struct {
    // Type is what the trigger opens: "dialog" (the default), "menu",
    // "listbox", "tree" or "grid" (the values of aria-haspopup). Another
    // value panics in dev mode with the closest valid one.
    Type string
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled overlay; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called
    // with the next state when the trigger or the overlay asks for a change:
    // for a controlled overlay it is how the change is asked for, for an
    // uncontrolled one a notification.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled makes the trigger inert and disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref, for a hook used together with others on the
    // same element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
    // OverlayRef is the overlay's ref, which the trigger's aria-controls
    // points to; the zero value makes the hook create its own. The hooks of
    // the overlay's element (UsePopover, UseDialog, UseFocusScope...) must
    // share it as their Ref option.
    OverlayRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

OverlayTriggerOptions configures [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger).

### type OverlayTriggerResult

```go
type OverlayTriggerResult struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the trigger: a press that toggles the overlay,
    // the "button" role, a tab stop, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and,
    // while the overlay is open, aria-controls. Override the role on an
    // element that is not a button.
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // OverlayProps go to the overlay's element when no other hook of the
    // element attaches the overlay's ref: they hold just that ref.
    OverlayProps tela.Prop
    // Open is the current state, controlled or not.
    Open bool
    // SetOpen asks for a state (a controlled overlay only reports it to
    // OnOpenChange), Toggle for the other one, and Close for closed; Open
    // for open is SetOpen(true).
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Toggle  func()
    Close   func()
    // Pressed is true while the trigger is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and OverlayRef the overlay's.
    Ref, OverlayRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

OverlayTriggerResult is what [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger) returns.

#### func UseOverlayTrigger

```go
func UseOverlayTrigger(o OverlayTriggerOptions) OverlayTriggerResult
```

UseOverlayTrigger holds the open state of an overlay and returns the props of its trigger (React Aria's useOverlayTrigger with useOverlayTriggerState): a press toggles the overlay, and the trigger says what it opens (aria-haspopup), whether it is open (aria-expanded) and which element it controls (aria-controls).

```go
trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{Type: "dialog"})
ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close, Dismissable: true})
return Fragment(
    Button(trig.TriggerProps, Class("rounded-md border px-3 py-1.5"), Text("Share")),
    Portal(If(trig.Open,
        Div(ov.Props, trig.OverlayProps, Role("dialog"), Text("Link copied")))))
```

The state is uncontrolled by default; pass Open for a controlled one. Pair it with [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) or [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay) and [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) for the overlay (sharing OverlayRef), and with [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger) for a menu.

**Example**

```go
// The trigger holds the state and says what it opens and whether it is
// open; OnOpenChange follows an uncontrolled overlay.
page := func() tela.Node {
    log, setLog := tela.UseState("")
    trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{
        Type:         "menu",
        OnOpenChange: func(open bool) { setLog.Set(fmt.Sprintf("open=%v", open)) },
    })
    return Div(
        Button(trig.TriggerProps, Text("Actions")),
        If(trig.Open, Div(Ref(trig.OverlayRef), Text("Items"))),
        Text(log))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions"))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions"), telatest.Expanded(true))
app.ExpectText("open=true")
fmt.Println("open=true")
// Output: open=true
```

### type PointerType

```go
type PointerType string
```

PointerType is the device or the way a press, or a hover, came from.

```go
const (
    // PointerMouse is a mouse or a touchpad.
    PointerMouse PointerType = "mouse"
    // PointerTouch is a finger on a touchscreen.
    PointerTouch PointerType = "touch"
    // PointerPen is a stylus.
    PointerPen PointerType = "pen"
    // PointerKeyboard is a press made with Enter or Space on the focused
    // element.
    PointerKeyboard PointerType = "keyboard"
    // PointerVirtual is a click that no pointer or key made: an assistive
    // technology or an agent (the "click" action of the semantics tree),
    // or the click a Label sends to the control it labels.
    PointerVirtual PointerType = "virtual"
)
```

The pointer types.

### type PopoverOptions

```go
type PopoverOptions struct {
    // Trigger is the ref of the element the popover is anchored to, the
    // trigger that opens it ([OverlayTriggerResult].Ref).
    Trigger tela.ElementRef
    // Open is whether the popover is open, and OnClose how it is closed:
    // see [OverlayOptions].
    Open    bool
    OnClose func()
    // Placement is where the popover goes around its trigger, one of
    // Floating UI's 12 placements such as "bottom-start"; "bottom" by
    // default. It flips to the opposite side when there is no room.
    Placement string
    // Offset is the distance in pixels between the trigger and the
    // popover.
    Offset float32
    // Floating are more options of [UseFloating], applied after the
    // popover's own (the placement, [Offset], [Flip] and [Shift] with 12 px
    // of room from the window's edges) and before the arrow's: a [Size]
    // that limits the height to the room available, say.
    Floating []FloatingOption
    // Modal makes the rest of the window inert while the popover is open,
    // as a menu does (React Aria's popovers are modal unless isNonModal
    // is set: here it is the other way round). A press on the trigger then
    // closes the popover, as it hits no element; a non-modal popover does
    // not close for the trigger's presses, which toggle it.
    Modal bool
    // KeyboardDismissDisabled keeps Escape from closing the popover.
    KeyboardDismissDisabled bool
    // ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside decides, for a press outside the popover
    // (and outside the popovers and dialogs opened from it), whether it
    // closes it; nil closes it for every press but the non-modal trigger's.
    ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside func(tela.PointerEvent) bool
    // Ref is the popover element's ref, for a hook used together with
    // others on the same element (the overlay trigger's OverlayRef, a
    // dialog); the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PopoverOptions configures [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover).

### type PopoverResult

```go
type PopoverResult struct {
    // Props go to the popover's element: it is fixed to the window and
    // placed next to the trigger in the frame that shows it, it is on the
    // overlay stack (Escape and presses outside close the top one), and
    // the ref. Render the element in a Portal.
    Props tela.Prop
    // ArrowProps go to an arrow element inside the popover, which points at
    // the trigger.
    ArrowProps tela.Prop
    // Placement is the placement the popover is in, after flipping; Side
    // and Align split it. They follow the engine by one frame: see
    // [Floating].
    Placement, Side, Align string
    // Ref is the ref attached to the popover's element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PopoverResult is what [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) returns.

#### func UsePopover

```go
func UsePopover(o PopoverOptions) PopoverResult
```

UsePopover returns the props of a popover (React Aria's usePopover): a floating element positioned by [`UseFloating`](#func-usefloating) next to its trigger, and dismissed by [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay): Escape, a press outside, or the focus going to another element closes it (never the trigger's press or focus, which toggle it). A press inside a popover opened from it, in a Portal or not, is inside.

```go
trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: trig.Ref, Ref: trig.OverlayRef, Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Offset: 4,
})
return Fragment(
    Button(trig.TriggerProps, Text("Filters")),
    Portal(Presence(If(trig.Open,
        Div(pop.Props, Exit("opacity-0"),
            Class("w-64 rounded-md border bg-popover p-4 shadow-md transition starting:opacity-0"),
            Div(pop.ArrowProps, Class("size-2 rotate-45 border bg-popover")),
            Text("Content"))))))
```

Put [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) on the same element, sharing the ref, when the popover holds a form or content to be read as a dialog.

**Example**

```go
// A popover 4 px below its trigger; a press outside it closes it.
page := func() tela.Node {
    trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{})
    pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
        Trigger: trig.Ref, Ref: trig.OverlayRef, Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close,
        Placement: "bottom-start", Offset: 4,
    })
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(trig.TriggerProps, Class("absolute left-4 top-4 h-8 w-24"), Text("Filters")),
        Portal(If(trig.Open,
            Div(pop.Props, TestID("pop"), Class("h-24 w-48 rounded-md border bg-white p-2"), Text("Content")))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Filters"))
r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("pop"))
fmt.Printf("popover at (%.0f, %.0f), %.0fx%.0f\n", r.X, r.Y, r.Width, r.Height)
app.ClickAt(350, 250)
app.ExpectNoText("Content")
fmt.Println("closed by a press outside")
// Output:
// popover at (16, 52), 192x96
// closed by a press outside
```

### type PressEvent

```go
type PressEvent struct {
    // PointerType is where the press came from.
    PointerType PointerType
    // X and Y are window coordinates; LocalX and LocalY are relative to the
    // element's border box.
    X, Y, LocalX, LocalY float32
    // Modifier keys held during the event; Meta is the Windows, Command or
    // Super key.
    Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Meta bool
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

PressEvent is passed to the callbacks of [`PressOptions`](#type-pressoptions). X and Y are the position of the event in the window, LocalX and LocalY relative to the border box of the element, in logical pixels; a press that no pointer made (keyboard, virtual) reports the center of the element.

Pressing stops the propagation of the events that make it (the pointer's, the key's, the click), as React Aria does, so a pressable card inside a pressable row presses only the card. Call [`PressEvent.ContinuePropagation`](#func-pressevent-continuepropagation) in a callback to let them bubble.

#### func (PressEvent) ContinuePropagation

```go
func (e PressEvent) ContinuePropagation()
```

ContinuePropagation lets the event that made this press bubble to the ancestors' handlers, instead of stopping it. It applies to the whole step of the press: if any of its callbacks continues, the event does.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var log []string
page := func() tela.Node {
    press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
        // Let the card's own handlers see the press too.
        OnPressStart: func(e aria.PressEvent) { e.ContinuePropagation() },
    })
    return Div(OnPointerDown(func() { log = append(log, "the card saw the pointer down") }),
        Button(press.Props, Text("Like")))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Like"))
fmt.Println(log)
// Output: [the card saw the pointer down]
```

### type PressOptions

```go
type PressOptions struct {
    // OnPressStart is called when a press begins: the pointer goes down on
    // the element, or Space goes down on it while it is focused. A press
    // that left the element (without [PressOptions.ShouldCancelOnPointerExit])
    // starts again if the pointer comes back while still held.
    OnPressStart func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressEnd is called when a press ends, whether it counts or not: the
    // release over the element, the pointer leaving it, the cancel of the
    // pointer or a lost focus.
    OnPressEnd func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressChange is called with true when a press starts and false when
    // it ends: the callback form of the Pressed field of the result.
    OnPressChange func(pressed bool)
    // OnPressUp is called when the pointer or the key is released over the
    // element, before OnPressEnd.
    OnPressUp func(PressEvent)
    // OnPress is called when the press completes: the release over the
    // element, Space released on it, Enter pressed on it, or a virtual
    // click. It does not run for a disabled element.
    OnPress func(PressEvent)
    // Disabled ignores every pointer, key and click on the element, and
    // ends a press in progress. It sets no prop: for a disabled look and
    // semantics use [UseButton] or h.Disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // ShouldCancelOnPointerExit ends the press for good when the pointer
    // leaves the element, instead of letting it start again when the
    // pointer comes back while pressed.
    ShouldCancelOnPointerExit bool
    // PreventFocusOnPress keeps the focus where it is when the pointer
    // goes down on the element (the default action of a press is to focus
    // the nearest focusable element).
    PreventFocusOnPress bool
    // Ref is the element's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element (see the package documentation); the zero
    // value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PressOptions configures [`UsePress`](#func-usepress).

### type PressResult

```go
type PressResult struct {
    // Props go to the element: the pointer, key, click and blur handlers
    // and the ref, merged. Props given after them in the element's
    // arguments override what they set, but handlers of the same event all
    // run.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Pressed is true while the element is pressed (a pointer is down on
    // it, or Space is held): style it with a class, since `active:` follows
    // the pointer only.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the ref attached to the element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PressResult is what [`UsePress`](#func-usepress) returns.

#### func UsePress

```go
func UsePress(o PressOptions) PressResult
```

UsePress returns the props that make an element pressable, the same across mouse, touch, pen and keyboard (React Aria's usePress).

```go
press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
    OnPress: func(e aria.PressEvent) { save() },
    Disabled: busy,
})
return Div(press.Props, Role("button"), TabIndex(0),
    Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5"), If(press.Pressed, Class("scale-95")), Text("Save"))
```

A press starts when the primary button, a touch contact or a pen tip goes down on the element. It ends when the pointer is released ([`PressOptions.OnPress`](#type-pressoptions) runs if that was over the element), leaves the element (which also ends it for good with [`PressOptions.ShouldCancelOnPointerExit`](#type-pressoptions)) or is cancelled: the system takes the touch, a touch becomes a scroll, or the element is unmounted. The element keeps receiving the pointer while it is pressed, wherever it goes.

With the keyboard, Enter on the focused element presses it at once (OnPressStart, OnPressUp, OnPressEnd and OnPress on the key down, never on a repeat), and Space starts the press on the key down and completes it on the key up; a press by Space ends without OnPress when the focus leaves the element. The hook prevents the default action of those keys (the click of a Button, the scroll of Space). A click that no pointer made (an assistive technology, an agent, a Label) is a virtual press.

The hook stops the propagation of the events that make a press (PressEvent.ContinuePropagation lets them bubble), prevents the default action of the click (a Button does not submit its Form), and does not run for a Disabled element.

The element needs no role: UsePress adds none. For a button use [`UseButton`](#func-usebutton), which adds the role, the tab stop and the disabled state.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
save := func() tela.Node {
    saved, setSaved := tela.UseState(0)
    press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
        OnPress: func(e aria.PressEvent) { setSaved.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) },
    })
    return Div(press.Props, Role("button"), TabIndex(0),
        Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5"), If(press.Pressed, Class("scale-95")),
        Textf("Saved %d times", saved))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, save)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Saved 0 times"))
app.Press("Enter") // the button has the focus after the click
app.Press("Space")
app.ExpectText("Saved 3 times")
fmt.Println("3 presses: mouse, Enter, Space")
// Output: 3 presses: mouse, Enter, Space
```

```go
type Rects struct {
    // Reference is the anchor's border box.
    Reference tela.Rect
    // Floating is the floating element's border box at the position the
    // middleware before Size left it at.
    Floating tela.Rect
}
```

Rects are the rectangles of the anchor and the floating element, in window coordinates.

### type SectionResult

```go
type SectionResult struct {
    // Props go to the element that groups the items: the "group" role,
    // named by the heading.
    Props tela.Prop
    // HeadingProps go to the heading's element, which only names the group
    // (role "presentation").
    HeadingProps tela.Prop
}
```

SectionResult is what [`Collection.Section`](#func-collectionk-section) returns.

### type SelectOptions

```go
type SelectOptions[K comparable] struct {
    Keys []K
    // TextValue is the text of an item: it is what the select shows when
    // the item is selected (SelectResult.Value) and what typeahead matches.
    // The default is fmt.Sprint of the key.
    TextValue         func(K) string
    DisabledKeys      []K
    Selected          Selection[K]
    DefaultSelected   Selection[K]
    OnSelectionChange func(Selection[K])
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled select; nil leaves it
    // to the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called with the
    // next state, as a request for a controlled select and as a
    // notification for an uncontrolled one.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Placeholder is what SelectResult.Value says while nothing is
    // selected.
    Placeholder string
    // Disabled makes the trigger inert and disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // Placement is where the popover goes around the trigger, one of
    // Floating UI's 12 placements; "bottom-start" by default. Offset is the
    // distance in pixels, and Floating are more options of [UseFloating] (a
    // [Size] that limits the height, say), as in [PopoverOptions].
    Placement string
    Offset    float32
    Floating  []FloatingOption
    // MatchWidth makes the popover as wide as the trigger (see
    // SelectResult.PopoverProps).
    MatchWidth bool
    // Modal makes the rest of the window inert while the list is open, as
    // React Aria's select does; see [PopoverOptions]. The default is a
    // non-modal popover.
    Modal bool
    // DisallowTypeAhead turns off typeahead, on the trigger and in the
    // list.
    DisallowTypeAhead bool
    // AriaLabel names the select when there is no label element; with
    // LabelProps the label element names it. The trigger's name is the
    // value followed by the name, as in React Aria ("Apple Favorite fruit").
    AriaLabel string
    // Ref is the trigger's ref, for a hook used together with others on the
    // same element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

SelectOptions configures [`UseSelect`](#func-useselect). The items are keyed like those of a list box: see [`ListBoxOptions`](#type-listboxoptions) for Keys, TextValue, DisabledKeys and the controlled and uncontrolled Selected, DefaultSelected and OnSelectionChange (a select holds one selected key).

### type SelectResult

```go
type SelectResult[K comparable] struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the trigger, a Button or any element: the press
    // that opens the list, the keys that open it (Enter, Space, ArrowDown
    // and ArrowUp) and change the selection while it is closed (typeahead
    // and ArrowLeft and ArrowRight), the "button" role, a tab stop,
    // aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-expanded, aria-controls while open
    // and aria-labelledby (the value and the label).
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // ValueProps go to the element inside the trigger that shows the
    // selected text (or the placeholder): the trigger is named by it.
    ValueProps tela.Prop
    // LabelProps go to the label element: it names the select, and a click
    // on it focuses the trigger.
    LabelProps tela.Prop
    // PopoverProps go to the popover's element, which holds the list
    // box: it is fixed to the window and placed next to the trigger in the
    // frame that shows it, it is on the overlay stack (Escape and a press
    // outside close it) and a focus scope gives the focus back to the
    // trigger when it unmounts. With MatchWidth it is as wide as the
    // trigger. Render it in a Portal, only while Open.
    PopoverProps tela.Prop
    // ArrowProps go to an arrow element inside the popover.
    ArrowProps tela.Prop
    // ListBox is the list: its Props go to the element that holds the
    // items (it scrolls) and ItemProps(k) to each item, as in [UseListBox].
    // The items are rendered inside the popover, only while Open.
    ListBox ListBoxResult[K]
    // Value is the text of the selected item, or the Placeholder.
    Value string
    // Selected is the current selection: [Selection.First] is the
    // selected key.
    Selected Selection[K]
    // Open is whether the list is open; SetOpen asks for a state, Toggle for
    // the other one and Close for closed.
    Open    bool
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Toggle  func()
    Close   func()
    // Pressed is true while the trigger is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Placement is the popover's placement after flipping (see
    // [PopoverResult]).
    Placement string
    // TriggerRef and PopoverRef are the refs of the trigger and the
    // popover.
    TriggerRef, PopoverRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

SelectResult is what [`UseSelect`](#func-useselect) returns.

#### func UseSelect

```go
func UseSelect[K comparable](o SelectOptions[K]) SelectResult[K]
```

UseSelect holds the state of a select and returns the props of its trigger, its popover and its list (React Aria's useSelect with useSelectState): a button that shows the selected item and opens a list box next to it. A press, Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the list (the last also with ArrowUp), the selected item or else the first (the last for ArrowUp) has the focus, choosing an item selects it, closes the list and gives the focus back to the trigger, and Escape closes it. On the closed trigger typing text selects the next item that starts with it and the left and right arrows select the previous and next item.

```go
sel := aria.UseSelect(aria.SelectOptions[string]{
    Keys: fruit, TextValue: capital, Placeholder: "Pick a fruit", MatchWidth: true,
})
return Fragment(
    Span(sel.LabelProps, Text("Favorite fruit")),
    Button(sel.TriggerProps, Class("flex w-48 justify-between rounded-md border px-3 py-2"),
        Span(sel.ValueProps, Text(sel.Value)), Icon(chevronDown)),
    Portal(If(sel.Open,
        Div(sel.PopoverProps, Class("rounded-md border bg-popover p-1 shadow-md"),
            Div(sel.ListBox.Props, Class("max-h-60 overflow-auto"),
                Range(len(fruit), func(i int) tela.Node {
                    k := fruit[i]
                    return Div(sel.ListBox.ItemProps(k), Key(k),
                        Class("rounded px-2 py-1.5 focus-visible:bg-accent aria-selected:font-medium"),
                        Text(capital(k)))
                }))))))
```

In the aria snapshot the closed select is a button named by its value and its label (`button "Banana Favorite fruit": Banana`), and the open list, a listbox named by the label, sits next to it.

The list lives in the component that calls the hook (its items are rendered by the caller only while open): the hook focuses the selected item when the list opens. There is no hidden native select, so a Form does not submit the value: read SelectResult.Selected in OnSubmit.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
names := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    sel := aria.UseSelect(aria.SelectOptions[string]{
        Keys: names, TextValue: capital, Placeholder: "Pick a fruit", MatchWidth: true,
    })
    return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-1 p-4"),
        Span(sel.LabelProps, Class("text-sm font-medium"), Text("Favorite fruit")),
        Button(sel.TriggerProps, Class("flex w-48 justify-between rounded-md border px-3 py-2"),
            Span(sel.ValueProps, Text(sel.Value))),
        Portal(If(sel.Open,
            Div(sel.PopoverProps, Class("rounded-md border bg-popover p-1 shadow-md"),
                Div(sel.ListBox.Props, Class("max-h-60 overflow-auto"),
                    Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
                        k := names[i]
                        return Div(sel.ListBox.ItemProps(k), Key(k),
                            Class("rounded px-2 py-1.5 focus-visible:bg-accent aria-selected:font-medium"),
                            Text(capital(k)))
                    }))))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("button", "Pick a fruit Favorite fruit"))
app.Press("ArrowDown") // opens it on the first item
app.Press("ArrowDown")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Enter") // selects Banana, closes and gives the focus back
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - text: Favorite fruit
// - button "Pick a fruit Favorite fruit": Pick a fruit
// - text: Favorite fruit
// - button "Pick a fruit Favorite fruit" [expanded]: Pick a fruit
// - listbox "Favorite fruit":
//   - option "Apple"
//   - option "Banana"
//   - option "Cherry"
// - text: Favorite fruit
// - button "Banana Favorite fruit": Banana
```

**Example (controlled)**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
names := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    sel, setSel := tela.UseState(aria.SelectionOf("banana"))
    s := aria.UseSelect(aria.SelectOptions[string]{
        Keys: names, TextValue: capital, AriaLabel: "Fruit",
        Selected: sel, OnSelectionChange: setSel.Set,
    })
    return Div(
        Button(s.TriggerProps, Span(s.ValueProps, Text(s.Value))),
        Portal(If(s.Open, Div(s.PopoverProps, Div(s.ListBox.Props,
            Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
                return Div(s.ListBox.ItemProps(names[i]), Key(names[i]), Text(capital(names[i])))
            }))))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Banana Fruit"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("option", "Cherry"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output: - button "Cherry Fruit": Cherry
```

### type Selection

```go
type Selection[K comparable] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Selection is an immutable set of keys, the selection of the collection hooks ([`UseListBox`](#func-uselistbox), [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu) and [`UseTabs`](#func-usetabs)): an explicit set of keys or [`All`](#func-all), React Aria's "all". Its methods never change the receiver, so a Selection can be kept in tela.UseState and shared freely.

```go
sel := aria.SelectionOf("b", "c")
sel.Has("b")              // true
sel.With("a").Keys()      // [b c a]
sel.Without("b").Keys()   // [c]
```

The zero Selection is "not given": a hook option left at it is uncontrolled, and the hook keeps the selection itself. Pass [`SelectionOf`](#func-selectionof) with no keys for a controlled, empty selection:

```go
// Uncontrolled: the hook keeps the selection.
aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{Keys: keys, SelectionMode: "multiple", DefaultSelected: aria.SelectionOf("b")}
// Controlled: the app keeps it.
sel, setSel := tela.UseState(aria.SelectionOf("b"))
aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{Keys: keys, SelectionMode: "multiple", Selected: sel, OnSelectionChange: setSel.Set}
```

A Selection is comparable with == (it holds a pointer), but two selections with the same keys are not == unless they are the same value: use [`Selection.Equal`](#func-selectionk-equal) to compare keys.

**Example**

```go
sel := aria.SelectionOf("banana", "cherry")
fmt.Println(sel.Has("banana"), sel.Has("apple"))
fmt.Println(sel.With("apple").Without("cherry"))
// Keys listed in the order of a collection:
fmt.Println(sel.In([]string{"apple", "banana", "cherry", "date"}))
// React Aria's "all", resolved against the keys:
fmt.Println(aria.All[string]().Resolve([]string{"apple", "banana"}))
// Output:
// true false
// {banana apple}
// [banana cherry]
// {apple banana}
```

#### func All

```go
func All[K comparable]() Selection[K]
```

All returns the selection of every key that can be selected: React Aria's "all". A collection hook shows every enabled key selected; its keys are not listed in the value, so [`Selection.Len`](#func-selectionk-len) is 0 and [`Selection.Keys`](#func-selectionk-keys) empty for it: use [`Selection.Resolve`](#func-selectionk-resolve) to turn it into the explicit keys of a collection.

#### func SelectionOf

```go
func SelectionOf[K comparable](keys ...K) Selection[K]
```

SelectionOf returns the selection of exactly the given keys (duplicates count once). With no keys it is the empty selection, which, unlike the zero Selection, is a value: it makes a controlled hook show nothing selected.

#### func (Selection[K]) Equal

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Equal(o Selection[K]) bool
```

Equal reports whether s and o select the same keys, whatever their order: two [`All`](#func-all) are equal, an [`All`](#func-all) and an explicit selection are not, and the zero Selection equals only itself.

#### func (Selection[K]) First

```go
func (s Selection[K]) First() (K, bool)
```

First returns the first key of an explicit selection, in the order the keys were added, and whether there is one: the key of a single selection.

#### func (Selection[K]) Has

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Has(k K) bool
```

Has reports whether k is selected. For [`All`](#func-all) it is always true (a hook still never selects a disabled key).

#### func (Selection[K]) In

```go
func (s Selection[K]) In(order []K) []K
```

In returns the selected keys among order, in the order of order: the selection of a collection listed in the order of its keys. For [`All`](#func-all) it is every key of order.

#### func (Selection[K]) IsAll

```go
func (s Selection[K]) IsAll() bool
```

IsAll reports whether s is [`All`](#func-all).

#### func (Selection[K]) IsEmpty

```go
func (s Selection[K]) IsEmpty() bool
```

IsEmpty reports whether no key is selected: the zero Selection and [`SelectionOf`](#func-selectionof) with no keys. [`All`](#func-all) is not empty.

#### func (Selection[K]) IsSet

```go
func (s Selection[K]) IsSet() bool
```

IsSet reports whether s is a selection. The zero Selection is not: it means "none given" in the options of the hooks (uncontrolled).

#### func (Selection[K]) Keys

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Keys() []K
```

Keys returns the keys of an explicit selection in the order they were added (nil for [`All`](#func-all) and the zero Selection). The slice is a copy. Use [`Selection.In`](#func-selectionk-in) to list them in the order of a collection.

#### func (Selection[K]) Len

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Len() int
```

Len returns the number of keys of an explicit selection. [`All`](#func-all) has no count of its own and returns 0: resolve it with [`Selection.Resolve`](#func-selectionk-resolve).

#### func (Selection[K]) Resolve

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Resolve(order []K) Selection[K]
```

Resolve returns s as an explicit selection of keys among order: for [`All`](#func-all) the keys of order, for an explicit selection s itself.

#### func (Selection[K]) String

```go
func (s Selection[K]) String() string
```

String returns "all", "unset" for the zero Selection, or the keys in braces.

#### func (Selection[K]) Toggle

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Toggle(k K) Selection[K]
```

Toggle returns s without k when it has it and with k when it does not.

#### func (Selection[K]) With

```go
func (s Selection[K]) With(keys ...K) Selection[K]
```

With returns s with the keys added. Adding to [`All`](#func-all) returns it as is.

#### func (Selection[K]) Without

```go
func (s Selection[K]) Without(keys ...K) Selection[K]
```

Without returns s with the keys removed. Removing from [`All`](#func-all) returns it as is, since it does not list its keys: resolve it first.

### type ShiftLimiter

```go
type ShiftLimiter struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ShiftLimiter limits how far [`Shift`](#func-shift) moves the element. Build one with [`LimitShift`](#func-limitshift); the zero value limits nothing.

#### func LimitShift

```go
func LimitShift(opts ...LimitShiftOptions) ShiftLimiter
```

LimitShift returns the limiter that keeps the element attached to the anchor while it shifts: the element stops following the window's edge when it would no longer touch the anchor (Floating UI's limitShift).

```go
aria.Shift(8, aria.ShiftOptions{Limiter: aria.LimitShift()})
```

### type ShiftOptions

```go
type ShiftOptions struct {
    // NoMainAxis stops the shift along the side's axis (the one that keeps
    // the element in view: x for the top and bottom sides; Floating UI's
    // mainAxis: false).
    NoMainAxis bool
    // CrossAxis also shifts it along the other axis, which would move it
    // into the anchor (crossAxis: true).
    CrossAxis bool
    // Limiter limits the shift; see [LimitShift].
    Limiter ShiftLimiter
}
```

ShiftOptions are the options of [`Shift`](#func-shift); the zero value is Floating UI's defaults.

### type SizeOptions

```go
type SizeOptions struct {
    // Padding is the space to keep between the element and the edges of
    // the area it must stay in.
    Padding float32
}
```

SizeOptions are the options of [`Size`](#func-size).

### type TabsOptions

```go
type TabsOptions[K comparable] struct {
    Keys         []K
    DisabledKeys []K
    // Orientation is "horizontal" (the default; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight
    // move between tabs) or "vertical" (ArrowUp and ArrowDown).
    Orientation string
    // KeyboardActivation is "automatic" (the default: the tab that has the
    // focus is selected, so the arrows change the panel) or "manual" (the
    // arrows move the focus and Enter or Space selects).
    KeyboardActivation string
    // Selected is the selected tab of a controlled list, as a [Selection]
    // of one key; the zero Selection leaves it to the hook, which starts
    // at DefaultSelected. A tab list always has one selected tab: the
    // first enabled one when none is given or the given one is missing or
    // disabled.
    Selected          Selection[K]
    DefaultSelected   Selection[K]
    OnSelectionChange func(Selection[K])
    Direction         string
    AriaLabel         string
    AriaLabelledBy    tela.ElementRef
    // Ref is the tab list's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

TabsOptions configures [`UseTabs`](#func-usetabs). The tabs are keyed like the items of a list box: see [`ListBoxOptions`](#type-listboxoptions) for Keys, DisabledKeys, Selected, DefaultSelected, OnSelectionChange, Direction, AriaLabel and AriaLabelledBy.

### type TabsResult

```go
type TabsResult[K comparable] struct {
    Collection[K]
    // Props go to the tab list's element: the "tablist" role,
    // aria-orientation, the ref and the key handler.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Selected is the selected tab (its [Selection.First] is the key).
    Selected Selection[K]
    // Ref is the ref attached to the tab list by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

TabsResult is what [`UseTabs`](#func-usetabs) returns.

#### func UseTabs

```go
func UseTabs[K comparable](o TabsOptions[K]) TabsResult[K]
```

UseTabs holds the state of a tab list and returns the props of the list, its tabs and its panels (React Aria's useTabList, useTab and useTabPanel with useTabListState).

```go
tabs := aria.UseTabs(aria.TabsOptions[string]{Keys: names, AriaLabel: "Settings"})
sel, _ := tabs.Selected.First()
return Div(
    Div(tabs.Props, Class("flex gap-1 border-b"),
        h.Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
            k := names[i]
            return Div(tabs.TabProps(k), Key(k),
                Class("px-3 py-2 aria-selected:border-b-2 aria-selected:border-primary focus-visible:ring-2"),
                Text(k))
        })),
    Div(tabs.PanelProps(sel), Class("p-4"), panel(sel)))
```

The arrow keys move the focus between tabs and go around the ends; Home and End jump; with the default automatic activation the focused tab is selected, with KeyboardActivation "manual" Enter or Space selects it. Disabled tabs are skipped. Only the selected tab is a tab stop: Tab goes from it to its panel.

**Example**

```go
names := []string{"account", "password"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    tabs := aria.UseTabs(aria.TabsOptions[string]{Keys: names, AriaLabel: "Settings"})
    sel, _ := tabs.Selected.First()
    return Div(
        Div(tabs.Props, Class("flex gap-1"),
            Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
                k := names[i]
                return Div(tabs.TabProps(k), Key(k), Class("px-3 py-2 aria-selected:border-b-2"), Text(k))
            })),
        Div(tabs.PanelProps(sel), Class("p-4"), Textf("%s settings", sel)))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page)
app.Press("Tab")
app.Press("ArrowRight")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - tablist "Settings":
//   - tab "account"
//   - tab "password" [selected]
// - tabpanel "password": password settings
```

#### func (TabsResult[K]) PanelProps

```go
func (r TabsResult[K]) PanelProps(k K) tela.Prop
```

PanelProps returns the props of the panel of the tab with key k: the "tabpanel" role, named by the tab, the ref that the tab's aria-controls points to, and a tab stop (give the panel TabIndex(-1) after Props when it holds focusable content of its own). Render the panel of the selected tab only.

#### func (TabsResult[K]) TabProps

```go
func (r TabsResult[K]) TabProps(k K) tela.Prop
```

TabProps returns the props of the tab with key k: the "tab" role, aria-selected, aria-controls (the panel, while selected), the ref, a tab stop on the selected tab (the arrows move between the others) and the handlers. It is [`Collection.ItemProps`](#func-collectionk-itemprops).

### type ToggleOptions

```go
type ToggleOptions struct {
    // Selected points to the state of a controlled control; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook.
    Selected *bool
    // DefaultSelected is the initial state of an uncontrolled control.
    DefaultSelected bool
    // OnChange is called with the next state when the user toggles the
    // control: for a controlled control it is how the change is asked for,
    // for an uncontrolled one a notification.
    OnChange func(selected bool)
    // OnPress is called when the control is pressed, before the state
    // changes; the other press callbacks are those of [PressOptions].
    OnPress func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressStart is called when a press begins.
    OnPressStart func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressEnd is called when a press ends, whether it counts or not.
    OnPressEnd func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressChange is called with true when a press starts and false when
    // it ends.
    OnPressChange func(pressed bool)
    // OnPressUp is called when the pointer or the key is released over the
    // control.
    OnPressUp func(PressEvent)
    // Disabled makes the control inert and disabled for styling and
    // assistive technologies (h.Disabled).
    Disabled bool
    // ReadOnly keeps the control focusable and readable but not
    // changeable (aria-readonly).
    ReadOnly bool
    // ID is the id of the element, for a Label's For; the default is one
    // made with tela.UseID, returned in the ID field of the result.
    ID string
    // Ref is the element's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element (see the package documentation); the zero
    // value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ToggleOptions configures [`UseToggleButton`](#func-usetogglebutton), [`UseCheckbox`](#func-usecheckbox) and [`UseSwitch`](#func-useswitch): a two-state control. Its state is uncontrolled when Selected is nil (the hook keeps it, starting at DefaultSelected) and controlled when Selected points to the caller's state: the control then shows it and only asks OnChange for the next value, as an Input with Value and OnChange does. OnChange is also called for an uncontrolled control, to follow it.

```go
// Uncontrolled: the hook keeps the state.
aria.ToggleOptions{DefaultSelected: true}
// Uncontrolled, and told of every change.
aria.ToggleOptions{DefaultSelected: true, OnChange: func(on bool) { save(on) }}
// Controlled: the caller keeps it.
on, setOn := tela.UseState(false)
aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &on, OnChange: setOn.Set}
```

To follow an uncontrolled control, read the Selected field of its result.

**Example**

```go
// An uncontrolled switch that tells the app about every change, and a
// controlled one: Selected points to the app's own state.
page := func() tela.Node {
    saved, setSaved := tela.UseState("none")
    on, setOn := tela.UseState(true)
    auto := aria.UseSwitch(aria.ToggleOptions{
        DefaultSelected: true,
        OnChange:        func(v bool) { setSaved.Set(fmt.Sprint(v)) },
    })
    manual := aria.UseSwitch(aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &on, OnChange: setOn.Set})
    return Div(
        Button(auto.Props, AriaLabel("Auto"), Class("h-6 w-11")),
        Button(manual.Props, AriaLabel("Manual"), Class("h-6 w-11")),
        Textf("auto saved: %s, manual: %v", saved, on))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("switch", "Auto"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("switch", "Manual"))
app.ExpectText("auto saved: false, manual: false")
fmt.Println("auto saved: false, manual: false")
// Output: auto saved: false, manual: false
```

### type ToggleResult

```go
type ToggleResult struct {
    // Props go to the element: the press, the role, the tab stop, the
    // checked or pressed state, the disabled and read-only states and the
    // ID.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Selected is the current state, controlled or not.
    Selected bool
    // Pressed is true while the control is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // ID is the element's id: ToggleOptions.ID, or one made by the hook.
    // A Label(For(id)) names the control and toggles it when clicked, if
    // the control is a Button element.
    ID string
    // Ref is the ref attached to the element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ToggleResult is what [`UseToggleButton`](#func-usetogglebutton), [`UseCheckbox`](#func-usecheckbox) and [`UseSwitch`](#func-useswitch) return.

#### func UseCheckbox

```go
func UseCheckbox(o ToggleOptions) ToggleResult
```

UseCheckbox returns the props of a checkbox (React Aria's useCheckbox): press (a click or a tap toggles it, and so does Space, but not Enter, as in HTML), the "checkbox" role, `aria-checked`, a tab stop, the disabled and read-only states and an ID for a Label. The `checked:` variant, and `peer-checked:` and `group-checked:`, match it while it is selected (so do `aria-checked:` and its peer and group forms).

```go
box := aria.UseCheckbox(aria.ToggleOptions{DefaultSelected: true})
return Div(Class("flex items-center gap-2"),
    Button(box.Props, Class("size-4 rounded border checked:bg-primary")),
    Label(For(box.ID), Text("Notifications")))
```

Render a checkbox with a Button, so that a Label can name it and toggle it when it is clicked: Tela's Label does that for an Input, a Textarea or a Button.

Selected, DefaultSelected and OnChange follow [`ToggleOptions`](#type-toggleoptions). There is no indeterminate state yet.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    box := aria.UseCheckbox(aria.ToggleOptions{DefaultSelected: true})
    return Div(Class("flex items-center gap-2"),
        Button(box.Props, Class("size-4 rounded border checked:bg-primary")),
        Label(For(box.ID), Text("Notifications")))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Click(telatest.ByText("Notifications")) // the Label toggles it
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - checkbox "Notifications" [checked]
// - text: Notifications
// - checkbox "Notifications"
// - text: Notifications
```

#### func UseSwitch

```go
func UseSwitch(o ToggleOptions) ToggleResult
```

UseSwitch returns the props of a switch (React Aria's useSwitch): the same as [`UseCheckbox`](#func-usecheckbox) with the "switch" role.

```go
sw := aria.UseSwitch(aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &on, OnChange: setOn.Set})
return Button(sw.Props, Class("h-6 w-11 rounded-full bg-muted checked:bg-primary"),
    Span(Class("block size-5 rounded-full bg-white transition checked:translate-x-5")))
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    on, setOn := tela.UseState(false)
    sw := aria.UseSwitch(aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &on, OnChange: setOn.Set})
    return Button(sw.Props, AriaLabel("Wi-Fi"), Class("h-6 w-11 rounded-full bg-muted checked:bg-primary"))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("switch", "Wi-Fi"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output: - switch "Wi-Fi" [checked]
```

#### func UseToggleButton

```go
func UseToggleButton(o ToggleOptions) ToggleResult
```

UseToggleButton returns the props of a button that is on or off (React Aria's useToggleButton): [`UseButton`](#func-usebutton) plus the state, shown as `aria-pressed`, so the `aria-pressed:` variants style it. Enter, Space, a click or a tap toggles it.

```go
bold, setBold := tela.UseState(false)
tb := aria.UseToggleButton(aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &bold, OnChange: setBold.Set})
return Button(tb.Props, Class("rounded px-2 aria-pressed:bg-accent"), Text("B"))
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    bold, setBold := tela.UseState(false)
    tb := aria.UseToggleButton(aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &bold, OnChange: setBold.Set})
    return Button(tb.Props, Class("rounded px-2 aria-pressed:bg-accent"), Text("Bold"))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Bold"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - button "Bold"
// - button "Bold" [pressed]
```

### type TooltipTriggerOptions

```go
type TooltipTriggerOptions struct {
    // Delay is how long the pointer must stay on the trigger before the
    // tooltip opens: [DefaultTooltipDelay] when zero, none with [NoDelay].
    // A tooltip opened by the keyboard focus has no delay, and neither
    // does one that opens while another tooltip is open or closed less than
    // CloseDelay ago (React Aria's warm-up and cool-down).
    Delay time.Duration
    // CloseDelay is how long the tooltip stays after the pointer leaves:
    // [DefaultTooltipCloseDelay] when zero, none with [NoDelay]. Moving to
    // the tooltip itself keeps it open.
    CloseDelay time.Duration
    // Disabled turns the tooltip off: it does not open.
    Disabled bool
    // Trigger is what opens the tooltip: "" for both the pointer hovering
    // and the keyboard focus (focus that a pointer press did not give), or
    // "focus" for the keyboard focus alone. Another value panics in dev
    // mode.
    Trigger string
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled tooltip; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called
    // with the next state: for a controlled tooltip it is how the change is
    // asked for, for an uncontrolled one a notification.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Ref is the trigger's ref, for a hook used together with others on
    // the same element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
    // TooltipRef is the tooltip element's ref, which the trigger's
    // aria-describedby points to; the zero value makes the hook create its
    // own.
    TooltipRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

TooltipTriggerOptions configures [`UseTooltipTrigger`](#func-usetooltiptrigger).

### type TooltipTriggerResult

```go
type TooltipTriggerResult struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the trigger: the hover, focus, key and pointer
    // handlers that open and close the tooltip, the ref, and, while the
    // tooltip is open, aria-describedby. The trigger keeps its own role and
    // tab stop: tooltips are for elements that are already focusable.
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // TooltipProps go to the tooltip's element, rendered while Open (in a
    // Portal, placed by [UseFloating] or [UsePopover]-like options): its
    // "tooltip" role, the ref, hover that keeps it open, and Escape, which
    // closes it before anything below it.
    TooltipProps tela.Prop
    // Open is whether the tooltip is open.
    Open bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and TooltipRef the tooltip's.
    Ref, TooltipRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

TooltipTriggerResult is what [`UseTooltipTrigger`](#func-usetooltiptrigger) returns.

#### func UseTooltipTrigger

```go
func UseTooltipTrigger(o TooltipTriggerOptions) TooltipTriggerResult
```

UseTooltipTrigger returns the props of a tooltip and of its trigger (React Aria's useTooltipTrigger and useTooltip, with useTooltipTriggerState): it opens when the pointer rests on the trigger or the keyboard focuses it, closes when either leaves, when the trigger is pressed or a key is typed on it, and with Escape.

```go
tip := aria.UseTooltipTrigger(aria.TooltipTriggerOptions{})
fl := aria.UseFloating(tip.Ref, aria.Placement("top"), aria.Offset(6), aria.Flip(), aria.Shift(8))
return Fragment(
    Button(tip.TriggerProps, Class("rounded-md border p-2"), Text("Save")),
    Portal(Presence(If(tip.Open,
        Div(tip.TooltipProps, fl.Props, Exit("opacity-0"),
            Class("rounded bg-foreground px-2 py-1 text-xs text-background transition starting:opacity-0"),
            Text("Saves the file (Ctrl+S)"))))))
```

The tooltips of a window behave as a group: opening one closes the others, and while one is open, or one closed less than [`DefaultTooltipCloseDelay`](#constants) ago, the next one opens at once. The delays run on the frame clock, with no goroutine, so an idle window with a tooltip pending or open asks for no frames.

**Example**

```go
// The tooltip opens 1.5 s after the pointer rests on its trigger, and
// closes half a second after it leaves.
page := func() tela.Node {
    tip := aria.UseTooltipTrigger(aria.TooltipTriggerOptions{})
    fl := aria.UseFloating(tip.Ref, aria.Placement("top"), aria.Offset(6), aria.Flip(), aria.Shift(8))
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(tip.TriggerProps, Class("absolute left-4 top-[100px] h-8 w-24"), Text("Save")),
        Portal(If(tip.Open,
            Div(tip.TooltipProps, fl.Props, Class("rounded bg-black px-2 py-1 text-xs text-white"), Text("Saves the file")))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(400, 300), telatest.NoSettle())
count := func() int { return app.Count(telatest.ByRole("tooltip", "Saves the file")) }
app.Hover(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"))
app.Advance(time.Second)
fmt.Println("after 1 s:", count())
app.Advance(600 * time.Millisecond)
fmt.Println("after 1.6 s:", count())
app.MouseMove(300, 250)
app.Advance(600 * time.Millisecond)
fmt.Println("0.6 s after leaving:", count())
// Output:
// after 1 s: 0
// after 1.6 s: 1
// 0.6 s after leaving: 0
```
